title: Cynthiana — Cynthia & Anna on the Licking
summary: Cynthiana, named for the sisters Cynthia and Anna, became the seat of Harrison County, carved from Bourbon and Scott in 1793 for Col. Benjamin Harrison.
bodyMarkdown:
Cynthiana, the seat of Harrison County, sits on the South Fork of the Licking River in northern Kentucky. The town and the county were both created in 1793, and their names come from two different Harrisons.

## Before the town

According to [Grokipedia's article on Cynthiana](https://grokipedia.com/page/Cynthiana,_Kentucky), the first European settlement in the area came in April 1775. That spring Captain John Hinkson led fifteen men from Pennsylvania to build a station of cabins on the South Fork, near a game trail known as the Buffalo Trace.

## A county and a town

An account of [Harrison County](https://grokipedia.com/page/harrison_county,_kentucky) says the county was formed on December 21, 1793, from parts of Bourbon and Scott counties. It was named for Colonel Benjamin Harrison, an early settler who had served as sheriff of Bourbon County. He also pressed for Kentucky statehood, helped frame its constitution and served in the legislature.

The county seat grew on a 150-acre tract donated by Robert Harrison, a local blacksmith. An account of [Cynthiana](https://grokipedia.com/page/Cynthiana,_Kentucky) says the town was named for his daughters, Cynthia and Anna. Early building centered on a courthouse and public square. Grokipedia says Cynthiana was formally incorporated as a town in 1802.

## Two Civil War battles

Kentucky stayed in the Union, but Cynthiana saw two battles during the Civil War. The first, on July 17, 1862, was part of Confederate General John Hunt Morgan's first cavalry raid into the state. Grokipedia says Morgan's men crossed the Licking, outflanked defenders fighting from houses and took the town in about two hours.

Morgan returned during his last Kentucky raid. On June 11, 1864, he and about 1,200 cavalrymen captured the town and its Union garrison. The garrison was five companies of the 168th Ohio Infantry and some local home guards. Morgan's men also captured nearly all of the 171st Ohio Infantry.

The next day Union forces defeated Morgan in the second battle, fought near Keller's Bridge.

## A river town

The South Fork of the Licking runs through Cynthiana and has flooded it many times. Grokipedia notes damage in the 1937 flood that struck the Ohio River basin and its tributaries.

## Kentucky today

Cynthiana is a home-rule city of 6,333 people as of the 2020 census, and it is still the seat of Harrison County. Grokipedia says its downtown holds one of Kentucky's largest groups of mid-1800s cast-iron commercial buildings. The restored Rohs Opera House hosts films, plays and concerts. Downstream on the same river system are [Falmouth at the Licking forks](/stories/falmouth-at-the-licking-forks/) and [Newport at the Licking mouth](/stories/newport-at-the-licking-mouth/).
